name: Hatita
overview: Hatita was a male member of the tribe of Levi, noted in Scripture for his descendants who returned to Judah after the Babylonian captivity. Beyond this significant detail, there are no additional notes or personal attributes recorded about him in the biblical text.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Hatita' appears in Ezra 2:42 and is presented as a proper name without any given meaning or divine origin. The biblical record does not provide further insight into the significance of this name.
familyAndRelationships: Hatita is identified as a descendant of Levi, linking him to the priestly tribe of Israel. Scripture specifically mentions his sons who returned from exile, but no other family relationships are recorded.
scriptureSignificance: Hatita's importance lies in his role as an ancestor whose descendants were part of the faithful remnant returning to Judah after captivity. This return signifies the restoration of the Levitical lineage and the continuation of worship and service to God in the post-exilic community. His mention in Ezra highlights the preservation of tribal identity during a pivotal moment in Israel's history.
